\section{Overview}

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Coordinate permutation of a decision tree]
\lean{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.permuteCoordinatesAux}
\label{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.permuteCoordinatesAux}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.castAvailable}
Let $\Omega$ and $\alpha$ be types, let $n$ be a natural number, let
$A\subseteq\mathrm{Fin}(n)$ be the available coordinates, and let $\sigma$ be a
permutation of $\mathrm{Fin}(n)$. The coordinate-permuted tree has available set
$\sigma(A)$; each query at coordinate $i$ becomes a query at $\sigma(i)$, with the same
label-dependent branches, recursively permuted.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation under coordinate permutation]
\lean{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.eval_permuteCoordinatesAux}
\label{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.eval_permuteCoordinatesAux}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.eval, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.eval_castAvailable, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.permuteCoordinatesAux}
\difficulty{4}
Let $A$ be a set of available coordinates among the $n$ coordinates, let $\sigma$ be a
permutation of those coordinates, and let $T$ be a finite decision tree with labels in
$\alpha$ and available coordinates $A$. For any input $x$ assigning an alphabet symbol
to each coordinate, evaluating the tree obtained by permuting $T$'s coordinates by
$\sigma$ equals evaluating $T$ at the input $i\mapsto x(\sigma(i))$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Query trace under coordinate permutations]
\lean{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.queryTrace_permuteCoordinatesAux}
\label{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.queryTrace_permuteCoordinatesAux}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.permuteCoordinatesAux, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.queryTrace, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.queryTrace_castAvailable}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\Omega$ be a set of coordinate values, and let
$\alpha$ be a set of leaf labels. Let $A$ be a set of available coordinates among the
$n$ coordinates, let $T$ be a finite decision tree over $\Omega$ with leaf labels in
$\alpha$ and available coordinates $A$, and let $\sigma$ be a permutation of the $n$
coordinates. For every input $x$, the query trace of the coordinate-permuted tree is
obtained by applying $\sigma$ to each coordinate in the query trace of $T$ on the input
$i\mapsto x(\sigma(i))$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Coordinate permutation of a decision tree]
\lean{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.permuteCoordinates}
\label{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.permuteCoordinates}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteAlphabetDecisionTree, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.castAvailable, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.permuteCoordinatesAux}
Let $\Omega$ and $\alpha$ be types, let $n$ be a natural number, let $\sigma$ be a
permutation of the coordinates $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $T$ be a finite decision tree
whose queries use those coordinates and whose branches are indexed by elements of
$\Omega$. The coordinate-permuted tree is the finite decision tree obtained by applying
the coordinate permutation to $T$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation under coordinate permutation]
\lean{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.eval_permuteCoordinates}
\label{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.eval_permuteCoordinates}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteAlphabetDecisionTree, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.eval, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.permuteCoordinates}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\sigma$ be a permutation of the $n$ coordinates, let $T$ be a finite-alphabet
decision tree on all $n$ coordinates with labels in $\alpha$, and let $x$ assign an
alphabet symbol to each coordinate. Evaluating the tree obtained by permuting the
coordinates of $T$ by $\sigma$ at $x$ equals evaluating $T$ at the input $i\mapsto
x(\sigma(i))$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Query trace under coordinate permutations]
\lean{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.queryTrace_permuteCoordinates}
\label{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.queryTrace_permuteCoordinates}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteAlphabetDecisionTree, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.permuteCoordinates, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.queryTrace}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\Omega$ be a set of coordinate values, and let
$\alpha$ be a set of leaf labels. Let $T$ be a finite decision tree with all $n$
coordinates available, let $\sigma$ be a permutation of those coordinates, and let $x$
assign a value in $\Omega$ to each coordinate. The query trace of the tree obtained by
permuting the coordinates of $T$ on input $x$ is the list obtained by applying $\sigma$
to each coordinate in the query trace of $T$ on the input $i\mapsto x(\sigma(i))$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coordinate permutation of query traces]
\lean{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.queries_permuteCoordinates_iff}
\label{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.queries_permuteCoordinates_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteAlphabetDecisionTree, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.Queries, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.permuteCoordinates, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.queryTrace_permuteCoordinates}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\Omega$ and $\alpha$ be types, let $\sigma$ be a
permutation of the $n$ coordinates, and let $T$ be a finite decision tree whose
available coordinates are all of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. For any coordinate $i$ and input
$x:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\Omega$, the permuted tree queries $i$ on $x$ if and only if $T$
queries $\sigma^{-1}(i)$ on the input whose value at $j$ is $x(\sigma(j))$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Query count under coordinate permutations]
\lean{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.queryCount_permuteCoordinates}
\label{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.queryCount_permuteCoordinates}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteAlphabetDecisionTree, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.permuteCoordinates, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.queryCount, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.queryTrace_permuteCoordinates}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $
Omega$ be a set of coordinate values, and let $
alpha$ be a set of leaf labels. A finite decision tree queries coordinates in
$\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, branching according to the observed coordinate value; let $T$ be
such a tree with all coordinates initially available, let $\sigma$ be a permutation of
the coordinates, and let $x$ assign a value in $\Omega$ to each coordinate. The number
of queries made by the tree obtained by permuting the coordinates of $T$ is the number
made by $T$ on the input whose value at coordinate $i$ is $x(\sigma(i))$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coordinate permutation preserves computation]
\lean{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.computes_permuteCoordinates}
\label{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.computes_permuteCoordinates}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.FiniteAlphabetDecisionTree, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.Computes, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.eval, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.eval_permuteCoordinates, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.permuteCoordinates, FABL.Sign, FABL.permuteInput}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\sigma$ be a permutation of the $n$ coordinates, and
let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ satisfy $f(x\circ\sigma)=f(x)$ for every input $x$. If a
decision tree over the sign alphabet computes $f$, then the tree obtained by permuting
its queried coordinates by $\sigma$ also computes $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Query probability under coordinate permutations]
\lean{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.deterministicQueryProbability_permuteCoordinates}
\label{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.deterministicQueryProbability_permuteCoordinates}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteAlphabetDecisionTree, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.deterministicQueryProbability, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.permuteCoordinates, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.queries_permuteCoordinates_iff, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.queryTrace, FABL.productMean, FABL.productMean_comp_permuteInput}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite alphabet, let $\pi$ be a probability distribution on $\Omega$,
and let $T$ be a finite decision tree on $n$ coordinates. For every permutation $\sigma$
of the coordinates and every coordinate $i$, the probability that the permuted tree
queries $i$ under independent inputs with common distribution $\pi$ equals the
probability that $T$ queries $\sigma^{-1}(i)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Average cost under coordinate permutations]
\lean{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.deterministicAverageCost_permuteCoordinates}
\label{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.deterministicAverageCost_permuteCoordinates}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteAlphabetDecisionTree, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.permuteCoordinates, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.queryCount, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.queryCount_permuteCoordinates, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.deterministicAverageCost, FABL.productMean, FABL.productMean_comp_permuteInput}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite alphabet, let $\pi$ be a probability distribution on $\Omega$,
and let $T$ be a finite decision tree on $n$ coordinates with outputs in $\alpha$. For
every permutation of the coordinates, the average number of queries of the permuted tree
under independent inputs distributed according to $\pi$ is equal to that of $T$.
\end{theorem}

\lean{FABL.booleanFunctionSymmetryGroup}

Let $f$ map the $n$-coordinate sign cube to the signs. Its symmetry group consists of
the permutations of the coordinates that leave $f$ unchanged on every input.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Transitivity of the symmetry group]
\lean{FABL.exists_booleanFunctionSymmetry_apply_eq}
\label{FABL.exists_booleanFunctionSymmetry_apply_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.IsTransitiveSymmetric, FABL.booleanFunctionSymmetryGroup}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be invariant under some coordinate permutation carrying
any specified coordinate to any other. Then, for every pair of coordinates $i,j$, a
symmetry of $f$ carries $i$ to $j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Symmetrized seed distribution]
\lean{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.symmetrizedSeedLaw}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p241-b006}
\label{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.symmetrizedSeedLaw}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree, FABL.Sign, FABL.booleanFunctionSymmetryGroup, FABL.uniformPMF}
Let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-coordinate sign cube, and let $T$ be a
randomized decision tree that computes $f$ for every seed. The symmetrized seed law on
pairs of a symmetry of $f$ and a seed of $T$ is obtained by choosing the symmetry
uniformly and the original seed according to its seed law, independently.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Expectation under the symmetrized seed law]
\lean{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.pmfExpectation_symmetrizedSeedLaw}
\label{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.pmfExpectation_symmetrizedSeedLaw}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.symmetrizedSeedLaw, FABL.Sign, FABL.booleanFunctionSymmetryGroup, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_bind, FABL.pmfExpectation_map, FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$, and let $T$ be a randomized decision tree with a finite
nonempty seed space, seed law, and deterministic trees that each compute $f$. Choose a
coordinate permutation uniformly from the symmetry group of $f$, independently of the
seed. For every real-valued function $g$ of the permutation and seed, its expectation
under this joint law equals the average over permutations of its expectation over the
seed law.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Symmetrized randomized decision tree]
\lean{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.symmetrization}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p241-b006}
\label{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.symmetrization}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.computes_permuteCoordinates, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.permuteCoordinates, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.symmetrizedSeedLaw, FABL.Sign, FABL.booleanFunctionSymmetryGroup}
Let $f$ be a Boolean function on the $n$-coordinate sign cube, and let $T$ be a
randomized decision tree that computes $f$ for every seed. The symmetrized tree uses a
seed consisting of a symmetry of $f$ and an original seed; it applies the corresponding
coordinate permutation to the selected tree and uses the joint law that chooses the
symmetry uniformly and the original seed according to its seed law. It still computes
$f$ for every seed.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Query probability as a seed average]
\lean{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.queryProbability_eq_seed_deterministicQueryProbability}
\label{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.queryProbability_eq_seed_deterministicQueryProbability}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.deterministicQueryProbability, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.queryProbability, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.queryProbabilityOnInput, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_comm, FABL.productMean}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite input alphabet with probability law $\pi$, and let $T$ be a
randomized decision tree with finite nonempty seed space. For any coordinate $i$, the
probability that $T$ queries $i$, when the input is drawn from the product law with
independent coordinates of law $\pi$, equals the seed-law average of the corresponding
probability for each deterministic tree selected by the seed.
\end{theorem}

Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a Boolean function on the sign cube ${\pm1}^n$,

\end{theorem}

\proofstep
  {FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.queryProbability_eq_seed_deterministicQueryProbability}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p230-b005,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p231-b005}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a Boolean function on the sign cube, let $T$ be
a randomized decision tree computing $f$ with sign-valued inputs and outputs, and let
$pi$ be a probability distribution on the sign alphabet. For each coordinate $i$, the
probability that the symmetrized tree queries $i$ under the independent product input
distribution is the average, over the uniform distribution on the permutation group
preserving $f$, of the query probability of $T$ at the coordinate obtained by applying
the inverse permutation to $i$.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.mem_booleanFunctionSymmetryGroup}
  {context}

\proofstep
  {FABL.exists_booleanFunctionSymmetry_apply_eq}
  {direct}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p045-b004}
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be invariant under a transitive group of coordinate
permutations, and let $T$ be a randomized decision tree computing $f$. For any
probability distribution $\pi$ on $\{-1,1\}$ and any coordinates $i,j$, the averages
over the uniform distribution on the permutation group preserving $f$ of the probability
that $T$ queries the permuted coordinate $\sigma^{-1}(i)$ and the probability that it
queries $\sigma^{-1}(j)$, in each case for an input drawn from the product distribution
with marginal $\pi$, are equal.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Equal query probabilities after symmetrization]
\lean{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.symmetrization_hasEqualQueryProbabilities}
\label{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.symmetrization_hasEqualQueryProbabilities}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.IsTransitiveSymmetric, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.HasEqualQueryProbabilities, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.symmetrization, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.symmetrization_queryProbability, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.symmetryAverage_queryProbability_eq, FABL.Sign}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a Boolean function on the sign cube whose
symmetries act transitively on the coordinates, and let $T$ be a randomized decision
tree computing $f$ with sign-valued inputs and outputs. For any probability distribution
$pi$ on the sign alphabet, the symmetrized tree has the same query probability at every
coordinate under the independent product input distribution.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Symmetrized query probability and average cost]

  {FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.symmetryAverage_queryProbability_eq}
  {context}

\proofstep
  {FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.symmetrization_hasEqualQueryProbabilities}
  {direct}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p231-b005,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p241-b006}
Let $n>0$, let $f$ be a Boolean function on the sign cube whose symmetries act
transitively on the coordinates, and let $T$ be a randomized decision tree computing $f$
with sign-valued inputs and outputs. For any probability distribution $pi$ on the sign
alphabet and any coordinate $i$, the probability that the symmetrized tree queries $i$
under the independent product input distribution equals the average cost of $T$ divided
by $n$.
\end{theorem}

Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be invariant under a
transitive group of coordinate permutations, and let $T$ be a randomized decision tree
that computes $f$ on every input. For any probability distribution $\pi$ on $\{-1,1\}$,
the revealment of the symmetrization of $T$ under the product input distribution with
marginal $\pi$ equals the average cost of $T$ under that distribution divided by $n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegativity of revealment]
\lean{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.revealment_nonneg}
\label{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.revealment_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.queryProbability, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.queryProbability_nonneg, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.revealment}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $Omega$ be a finite input alphabet, and let $T$ be a
randomized decision tree on $n$ coordinates with a finite nonempty seed space and a
probability law on its seeds, such that every seed-selected tree computes the same
function. For any probability distribution $pi$ on $Omega$, the revealment of $T$
under the independent product input distribution is nonnegative.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Average cost in dimension zero]
\lean{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.averageCost_zero_dimension}
\label{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.averageCost_zero_dimension}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.averageCost, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.sum_queryProbability_eq_averageCost}
\difficulty{3}
Let the input alphabet be finite, let the output alphabet be arbitrary, and let a
randomized decision tree act on inputs with zero coordinates. For every probability
distribution on the input alphabet, its average query cost is zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Revealment in zero dimensions]
\lean{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.revealment_zero_dimension}
\label{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.revealment_zero_dimension}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.revealment}
\difficulty{1}
Let $Omega$ be a finite alphabet, let $T$ be a randomized decision tree on zero
coordinates with a finite nonempty seed space and a probability law on its seeds, and
let $pi$ be any probability distribution on $Omega$. Then the revealment of $T$ under
the independent product input distribution is zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Average complexity is bounded by average cost]
\lean{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.averageComplexity_le_averageCost}
\label{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.averageComplexity_le_averageCost}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.averageComplexity, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.averageCost, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.averageCost_nonneg}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite alphabet, let $\alpha$ be an output type, let $n$ be a
nonnegative integer, let $g:(\mathrm{Fin}\,n\to\Omega)\to\alpha$, and let $\pi$ be a
probability distribution on $\Omega$. For any zero-error randomized decision tree
computing $g$, the infimum of the average costs over all such trees is at most the
average cost of that tree under independent inputs drawn from $\pi$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Function revealment bound]
\lean{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.functionRevealment_le_revealment}
\label{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.functionRevealment_le_revealment}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.functionRevealment, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.revealment, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.revealment_nonneg}
\difficulty{4}
Let the input alphabet be finite, let $g$ be a function on length-$n$ inputs over that
alphabet, let $\pi$ be a probability distribution on the alphabet, and let $T$ be a
randomized decision tree computing $g$. The infimum of revealment over all randomized
decision trees computing $g$ is at most the revealment of $T$ under the product input
distribution with marginal $\pi$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegativity of function revealment]
\lean{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.functionRevealment_nonneg}
\label{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.functionRevealment_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.completeTree, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.completeTree_computes, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.functionRevealment, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.ofDeterministic, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.revealment, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.revealment_nonneg}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $Omega$ be a finite set, let $alpha$ be a type,
let $pi$ be a probability mass function on $Omega$, and let $g:(Fin
ntoOmega)toalpha$ be any function. The infimum, over all zero-error randomized
decision trees computing $g$, of their revealment under the product input distribution
induced by $pi$ is nonnegative.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Zero complexity in dimension zero]
\lean{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.averageComplexity_zero_dimension}
\label{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.averageComplexity_zero_dimension}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.completeTree, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.completeTree_computes, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.averageComplexity, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.averageComplexity_le_averageCost, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.averageComplexity_nonneg, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.averageCost_zero_dimension, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.ofDeterministic}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\\Omega$ be a finite alphabet with probability distribution $\\pi$, let $\\alpha$
be any output set, and let $g:(\\mathrm{Fin}\,0\\to\\Omega)\\to\\alpha$. The minimum
average query complexity of a finite randomized decision tree computing $g$ is zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Zero revealment in dimension zero]
\lean{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.functionRevealment_zero_dimension}
\label{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.functionRevealment_zero_dimension}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.completeTree, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.completeTree_computes, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.functionRevealment, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.functionRevealment_le_revealment, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.functionRevealment_nonneg, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.ofDeterministic, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.revealment_zero_dimension}
\difficulty{4}
Let $Omega$ be a finite set, let $alpha$ be a type, let $pi$ be a probability mass
function on $Omega$, and let $g:(Fin 0toOmega)toalpha$ be any function. The
infimum of the revealments of zero-error randomized decision trees computing $g$ is $0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Revealment and average complexity]
\lean{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.functionRevealment_eq_averageComplexity_div}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p241-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p230-b005
}
\label{FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.functionRevealment_eq_averageComplexity_div}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.completeTree, FABL.FiniteDecisionTree.completeTree_computes, FABL.IsTransitiveSymmetric, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.averageComplexity, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.averageComplexity_le_averageCost, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.averageComplexity_zero_dimension, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.averageCost, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.averageCost_le_card_mul_revealment, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.functionRevealment, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.functionRevealment_le_revealment, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.functionRevealment_zero_dimension, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.ofDeterministic, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.revealment, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.symmetrization, FABL.RandomizedDecisionTree.symmetrization_revealment_eq_averageCost_div, FABL.Sign}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ be invariant under a
transitive action of coordinate permutations, and let $\pi$ be a probability
distribution on $\{-1,1\}$. Then the infimum, over randomized decision trees computing
$f$, of their revealment under the product input distribution with marginal $\pi$ equals
the corresponding infimum of average query costs divided by $n$.
\end{theorem}
